questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was just very difficult. I honestly don't really have any recommendations. I ended up renting an AirBnB half of the time and rented an apartment by someone I know during the second half of the semester

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I is really fun to live off campus. You get a really good feeling of what it means to be a local which is something that I personally really wanted to experience

Additional comments:

questions.answer: I'm not completely sure what is meant by this, but generally I found it quite easy

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an email contact to reach out to and they answered very quickly every time

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready at the exact time where the course registration opens - otherwise you might not get the courses you want

Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took bachelor level courses and they were not too difficult. However there were a lot of deadlines throughout the semester

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are higher expectations to students' active participation in classes and there were student presentations in every class

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Comparative Politics (13277)
The Euro, migration and climate change: European challenges and opportunities (13539)
Europe's Foreign and Security Policies (18044)
Introduction to American Politics (16696)
How the Media Works (18962)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the course 'How the Media Works (18962)'. The professor was very engaging and energetic which made the classes really fun to be a part of

Additional comments:

questions.answer: There were a lot of social and sports clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going to a lot of different museums. It is free for EU citizens under 26 years old

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going to other cities in France. I went to Bordeaux during my exchange and the culture seems very different in Paris compared to other cities in France, which is fun to experience

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural differences challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Parisians love sitting a cafes and just chilling outside - I really enjoyed that atmosphere

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. It is important to attend to the social activities provided by the host institution
2. Don't be afraid to practice your French 
3. Don't get too caught up the the academic work and remember to enjoy just being in a foreign city, since the academic environment is very demanding

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think that I listed the most important points already

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to practice and getting better at French

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was finde a work/life balance

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
